You'll have the opportunity to help us showcase our libraries in sample apps, making complex topics easier to use. jobs.title: Principal Product Manager
jobs.description: Job Description AI Frontiers is building an enterprise process intelligence platform that combines operating procedures, system evidence, process data, controls, and practitioner knowledge to show how work actually runs. It helps operations teams identify high-value opportunities, redesign priority processes, define controls, and measure outcomes against a baseline. The platform is intended to support transformation across operations portfolios. The Principal Product Manager will own the platform's product direction and product operating model. You will bring operations leaders, practitioners, risk partners, and engineers into one product process so the team builds against defined problems and measurable outcomes. You will be accountable for the product backlog, customer discovery, sponsor onboarding, release outcomes, and adoption. Operations teams will continue to own their transformation decisions, delivery, role changes, and realized benefits. Your job is to make the platform useful enough, clear enough, and evidence-based enough for those teams to make and execute those decisions. WHAT WILL YOU DO? • Set the product vision, strategy, operating model, and outcome roadmap, including the evidence needed to continue, change, stop, or transfer the product • Lead discovery with operations leaders, practitioners, control partners, and delivery teams, turning their problems into opportunities with clear scope, baselines, success measures, and accountable owners • Own and order the backlog across discovery, triage, process decomposition, target-state design, control architecture, measurement, and role-impact analysis • Define release outcomes and acceptance criteria, making scope and sequencing decisions when time, data, or capacity is constrained • Define how the platform sizes opportunities, assesses readiness, ranks work, and presents evidence to investment and transformation decision makers • Shape the user experience, onboarding, documentation, and learning paths so operations leaders, analysts, practitioners, risk partners, and delivery teams can use the platform effectively • Own product measures and reviews covering process coverage, time to baseline, validated opportunity, adoption, designs funded, time to value, and realized outcomes • Set the partner strategy for process mining, benchmarks, taxonomies, transformation methods, and skills data based on customer need and product economics • Coordinate dependencies and approvals across risk, compliance, privacy, architecture, data, platform, automation, and HR, then prepare quarterly investment, capacity, and operating-model decisions WHAT DO YOU NEED TO SUCCEED? Must have: • 8+ years of product management, product ownership, or related experience, including responsibility for an enterprise product through discovery, delivery, adoption, and measurement • Experience working closely with engineering leaders on data, workflow, analytics, automation, or AI products • Strong product judgment: you can separate a user request from the underlying problem, choose what the team will not build, and explain the trade-off • Experience running customer discovery with operational users and senior sponsors whose needs, incentives, and measures differ • Ability to define baselines, business cases, product measures, and acceptance criteria for complex enterprise work • Experience managing a backlog across technical dependencies, customer commitments, risk requirements, and limited capacity • Comfort working with incomplete or conflicting process evidence and turning it into testable product decisions • Experience navigating privacy, security, risk, compliance, architecture, and data-governance requirements • Clear written and verbal communication with practitioners, engineers, control partners, and executives • A record of building trust across teams without taking ownership away from the business or delivery groups accountable for results Nice-to-have: • Experience with process intelligence

You'll own revenue for APILayer's largest API group, led by ipstack, and the shared platform every APILayer API runs on. Customers buy through three storefronts: each API's own site (such as ipstack.com and fixer.io), the APILayer Marketplace, and the new APILayer ecosystem, where one account buys many APIs.
